title: dynamic-scratch-reuse-and-fanout-aware-kernel-selection-to-reduce-peak-gpu-workspace
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: observed high peak GPU workspace usage for mixed-sequence inference (short+long requests) and multi-query fanout workloads. Existing arena tuning + static activation checkpointing provided good average memory savings but left headroom in two patterns: (1) transient scratch buffer spikes from kernels that allocate per-op temp buffers, and (2) suboptimal kernel choices when the operator fanout (key/value heads * queries) changes runtime characteristics. This PR implements two complimentary mechanisms to reduce peak workspace: 1) dynamic scratch reuse: a runtime scratch allocator that tracks short-lived temp regions by lifetime buckets and reuses buffers across operators within the same execution frame, avoiding repeated allocations and reducing fragmentation; 2) fanout-aware kernel selection: extend the kernel-selector to consider request fanout and KV cache reshaping costs when choosing between tiled/packed attention kernels and the low-memory fused attention kernels.

Summary of changes: implemented a lightweight scratch manager in runtime/scratch_manager.{cpp,h} with a lock-free free-list per-sizeclass and lifetime-tagging. Hooked the scratch allocation path into the kernel interface and modified critical kernels (attention, rotary, layernorm) to request scratch via the manager. Added a fanout heuristic in runtime/kernel_selector.cpp that uses observed Q*K fanout counters (collected per-model) to pick kernels that trade compute for lower transient memory. Added a compatibility path so that models pinned to older kernel profiles will continue to run the legacy selector. Integrated unit and microbenchmarks under benchmark-lab/ with a new benchmark script fanout_memory_profile.py and an end-to-end e2e memory test that simulates interleaved short/long requests.

Performance results: on A100-40GB with GPT-2 style model (1B params) and mixed workload (50% seq_len=32, 50% seq_len=1024) peak workspace dropped from 16.8GB to 12.1GB (~28% reduction). For high-fanout Q=16 tests the transient peak reduced by ~34% when the fanout-aware kernel was selected. End-to-end latency impact: median latency for long requests increased ~2.3% in a worst-case knob-on scenario where the low-memory kernel is used; this is within the SLA tradeoff and we expose a config flag to prefer latency vs memory at policy-level.

Compatibility and rollout strategy: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.scratch_reuse.enabled=false by default in this PR; we plan a phased rollout: enable on non-production clusters for 2 weeks, then opt-in for Dedicated clusters with memory pressure, finally flip default after one week of metrics monitoring. Kernel selection heuristic is additive and can be disabled with runtime.kernel_selector.fanout_heuristic=false. Added telemetry metrics: runtime.scratch_reuse.alloc_reuse_ratio, kernel_selector.fanout_decision_count and memory.scratch_peak_by_model.

Testing: added unit tests for scratch manager lifecycle and size-class reuse; added integration tests that assert no OOM on synthetic high-fanout scenarios; ran infra e2e-bench and observed stable results. CI: linux-unit-tests, cuda-smoke, and e2e-bench run green in the final run. Created a small fuzz harness to ensure lifetime tagging prevents use-after-free across frames.

Backward compatibility: no breaking API changes; the kernel interface signature extended with an optional scratch_token but remains backward-compatible with default nullptr behavior. Documentation: runtime/README.md updated with configuration knobs, and redwood-docs/ops/gpu-memory-tuning.md includes recommended settings for Dedicated customers.

Notes: this PR intentionally avoids changing global arena sizing heuristics in this iteration — that will be a follow-up to measure impact of scratch reuse on arena fragmentation (ENG-1919). Also, we identified a secondary opportunity to compress KV cache layout when fanout>8; tracked separately under ENG-1875.

release_notes: Reduced peak GPU workspace by ~28% for mixed short/long workloads via dynamic scratch buffer reuse.
Added fanout-aware kernel selection which reduces transient memory for high-query fanout workloads.
Exposed runtime knobs to tune memory vs latency tradeoffs: runtime.scratch_reuse.enabled and runtime.kernel_selector.fanout_heuristic.
